To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

power converters are the key enabling component of wind turbines, that the cost of the power converter system is a major contributor to the cost of the wind turbine, and that the power converter technology is a critical factor in determining the reliability of wind turbines.

the power converter technology is evolving to higher power and higher power density and reliability, and that the power converter is becoming more and more a key element of the overall wind turbine system.

medium-voltage power electronics converters are a promising power converter technology for wind turbines, and they are expected to be the dominant power converter configuration for the next generation wind turbines, with the main challenges being the cost and reliability of such power converter technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) power converters for large wind turbine systems (MW level); (2) power converters for medium-voltage wind turbine systems (kW-MW level); (3) power converter topologies for medium-voltage systems; and (4) power converter control strategies for medium-voltage applications.
the design, analysis, and control of power electronics converters for wind turbine applications.
the development of a new type of power converter that can meet these needs and that is based on the use of medium-voltage power devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future of wind turbines is medium-voltage multilevel power converters.

there is no one single power converter technology for the future, but rather a combination of different technologies, which are selected according to the power and voltage level, the power quality, and the cost and reliability requirements.

power converters will evolve toward full power conversion and medium-voltage technology, but with an increasing number of topologies, which will be selected based on the specific wind turbine configuration and the specific wind turbine manufacturer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the power converters are a key technology in the future wind turbine systems.
power converter technologies are evolving and the future will see more power electronics converters in wind turbines, and also more and more medium-voltage power electronics converters in the future.
the power converter technology for large wind turbines is at a turning point where a number of new technologies are under development and will soon be commercialized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no magic solutions, and the best solution is the one that is the most suitable to the specific application.
there is a need to develop a more robust, cost-effective, and reliable power converter for medium-voltage wind turbines.
the future wind turbines will be dominated by power converters with power level of 1–2 MW per unit and medium voltage level of 1.5–3 kV.
